text:
cory: Heads-up — saw a Dedicated tenant hit its reserved throughput ceiling and then have requests dropped even though other tenants in the pool had spare capacity. Repro: small spike + background batch from same org. Anyone run into this?

maria: Was the org pinned to a GPU pool or routing-by-cost? If pinned, it should be isolated. Can you paste the allocation / quota output?

cory: Pasting quick dump:```
$ rctl show --org acme
reserved_throughput: 5000
used: 5000
burst_credit: 0
shared_pool_available: 12000
inflight_limit: 200
policy: pin_to_pool
```
requests after this stayed at 5000/s but new ones returned 429s instead of borrowing from shared_pool. :confused:

kevin: That looks like enforcement ordering. My mental model: quota_enforcer checks per-org reserved_quota and inflight_count first, and only if reserved < req it tries shared pool. If inflight_count is hit early it can short-circuit before shared-pool check. I *think* there's a path where inflight is enforced prior to fallback accounting which would lead to these 429s.

jamie: Yup saw a similar pattern during canary-1. Patch we had locally changed ordering to evaluate fallback eligibility *before* rejecting on inflight, then re-check inflight once borrowing decided. That allowed borrowing to proceed but still limited bursts.

opt-bot: Suggestion captured: add a telemetry label `quota.fallback_origin` with values {none,reserved,shared,overflow} and emit when a request transitions. Helps debug noisy neighbor situations. Example: `quota.event{org="acme", fallback_origin="shared"}`

sre-bot: Incident INC-5592 created for "Dedicated tenant 429s when shared pool available" assigned to @kevin. Priority: P2. Link: https://incidents.internal/INC-5592

maria: Also worth noting customers see this as reliability — we should reflect it in Console: show "shared pool usage by pool" on the tenant page and an estimated time-to-availability when reserved exhausted. That reduces tickets.

cory: I'll draft an RFC with repro steps + perf numbers. Quick question: is changing enforcement ordering considered safe for rolling deploy? any unstated edge-cases (e.g., double-charging burst credits)? :thinking_face:

kevin: Should be safe if we: 1) gate behind feature flag 2) add e2e that simulates spike + background batch 3) ensure atomicity when borrowing (use existing token-bucket update path). Main risk is double-debit on retry — we'll add idempotency key check. I'll start a branch.

jamie: For rollout UX: add a console toggle per-dedicated-pool to opt into "aggressive fallback" for customers willing to trade isolation for availability. default off. We can then flip for a couple of tenants in staging.

cory: Perfect. I'll include a short runbook for rollback (flip feature flag + remap routes). Assigning followups: KEVIN -> quota_enforcer PR, JAMIE -> console toggle mockups, MARIA -> telemetry dashboard panel.

kevin: Taking it. Will put PR link here when ready.

opt-bot: Recommendation: also add metric `quota.borrowed_tokens_total` and a tag `borrowed_from_pool` so billing/optimize can decide whether to recommend Dedicated capacity increases.

cory: Nice. Thanks y'all — will ping when RFC is up.
